Great game.  My buddy was a huge fan of the first Remnant game.  I had never heard of it.  (though, I had it in my library from a Humble Bundle some time ago).  He has been trying to get our group of friends to get it.  I was the first one to get it.  It is enjoyable.  It is my first Souls-like game.  I don't like punishing games.  This one isn't too bad, at least Co-Op.  Single player, is an ENTIRELY different story.  I generally just play around in Single Player to get some resources, and wait for my buddy to play Co-Op for the meat of the game.

The story is very rich, and interesting.  I wish there was an off-line reading mode for all of the books and to help make the story a bit more coherent.  I really wish it had an app that kept track of things (like the story) but also load-outs.  When playing the game co-op, I want to see more of the story, my buddy doesn't.  I'd love to go back and see what was said, read, etc.  

This brings us to problem one.  I have completed 1 world, and am probably through about 50% or more of the second (plus finished the Labyrinth).  You get a lot of "stuff". Rings, Weapons, Amulets, Relic Shards.  Just a lot.  It needs a way to filter.  It really lacks that.  It would be nice to play around with loadouts "offline" say, via an official app.  It would be really nice to be able to load them by touching a stone.  These are Quality of Life improvements that would really help.  Just the ability to filter items in-game would be an amazing amount of help.  Maybe a list of items and what they do, instead of having to go and click on each one in a grid as well.

Problem two - for those like me.  If you like a specific weapon, and only want to use that, that is good, because of difficulty scaling, you can completely out-scale your build.  I've already maxed out one class, and that makes using 2 classes without one maxed out, difficult.  More-so than when I started out.  From what I have been reading, the problem gets worse, with it becoming increasingly difficult to get lower level materials to level up lower guns you may want to try to just the power curve going up.  It does not seem that the playstyles of focus everything on one build and wanting to try everything are very compatible with each other, in this game when you reach a mid-game type point.  

Now, neither of my "problems" are show-stoppers, or honestly, big deals in the long run.  So far, I've avoided bugs, mostly.  I've gotten stuck in walls/floors a few times.  One time, I even needed to exit the game and come back in.  There are times you are "marked" as in combat, when you are not.  I have a hunter, and have used hunter mark to find bad guys in the walls or not activated.  No way to engage them, and I couldn't interact with the stones.  That is more of an annoyance.  

The game also suffers from an issue where some keys are "hard-coded".  I can adjust most keys, but one in particular, Surrender is not able to be modified.  I use ESDF instead of WASD.  So, it seems that most of the time when I go down and try to crawl into a better spot to be revived, I end up surrendering instead.  I would even be ok with knowing what to bind the settings manually to fix it.  Again, annoyance, but all games should let you modify all keys.  

I know I have a lot of complaints, but really, this is a terrific game.  Buy it.  I picked up the upgraded version so I would get the DLC.  I am very happy I did. I love the ability to collect various classes and have them interact with each other.   I like that there are so many very unique weapons.  I like the very unique looks and feels of the worlds.  I like how the game actually caters to various play styles with being able to put together 2 classes to create a uniquely named archetype.  There is a LOT to like about this game.  I highly recommend it.  It is MUST BUY if you like to play Co-Op.  Just watch where you are firing, since the game has friendly fire.  The Handler class lets you mitigate up to 80% of that damage at level 10, which is really nice.  

Just a note, you can group up to 3 players n co-op.

Truly spectacular sequel. I waited to post a review as my system was plagued by crashes and visual glitches initially. Thankfully these issues have mostly stopped. As a fan of the Fromsoft secret sauce, Remnant 2 captures what matters most to me. The game play is fast, brutal, and engaging. The exploration is very rewarding with incredible itemization. The environment/art direction is beautiful. The story is vague but serviceable. Overall it has been a delight to play this game and I hope Gunfire games can continue to create the ultimate "dark souls with guns" experience in the future.
Important note to Intel Arc users: Download the beta for Arc A750. I use an A770 but the beta fixed major issues regarding graphical performance

The gameplay is ok very much souls style with guns.
The classes are alright and the variety is ok.

But realistically your stuck picking one gun to play the whole game through with and 2 classes.
Also they CONTINUE to focus on nerfing or removing farming methods in a single player grindy game.

Switching off takes a long time to get them up to level without "cheating".
The developer has hidden a majority of the items in secret rooms and areas which some have convoluted solutions you wouldn't ever think of. So your going to miss out on a lot of items, weapons and archtypes without a guide.

The enemies have a small amount of variety but their AI literally all do the same thing. 

Melee and close range weapons can't be used effectively against some bosses and enemies so your build may be made non viable. Plus it's a bit harder when enemies are bum rushing you and you can't kill them fast enough.

1 secondary gun has the BEST aoe clear in the game and as such for the way the enemies function everyone basically has to use it. 

Enemies can spawn out of nowhere and in some cases they just infinitely spawn making it nearly impossible to continue or focus on the bigger enemies. 

All in all it's an ok game

Edit: Hunting for items can be a pain with randomized worlds, events and locations....though items are always in the same locations when there.

The story is a tiny thread just like any Dark Souls game. Each boss and event has a mini story to them but not all that much. Your character is a bit of a nobody.
